reuse.why: The tree already has getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts deciding a schedule's expected amount, yet the change neither updates nor calls it and instead writes the new worst-case rule inline at each site it touches.

duplication.why: The same missing/approx/range nested ternary (with getApproxNumberThreshold and Math.min) is written three times, in api-models.ts, forecast-schedules.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, alongside the untouched midpoint copies.

placement.why: The amount rule belongs in the shared schedules helper; it is instead embedded in the API mapper, the forecast normaliser and the preview function.

scope.why: Edits stay on schedule amount computation, the API field and tests, with no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: The rule now exists in three inline copies while getScheduledAmount, schedules/app.ts (two sites) and schedule-template.ts still use the old midpoint, so the codebase disagrees with itself and every future rule change must touch many places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions compute the amount inline instead of through shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount is left unchanged (still midpoint) while api-models.ts toExternal, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions each carry their own worst-case implementation
